description:
The HTTP server stops keeping its own error-to-status mappings and projects the library's failure classification into a status.

## Background

`crates/server/src/routes.rs` handlers return `Result<Json<T>, StatusCode>`. `path_read_error_status` maps `PathReadError` (NotFound/CommitNotFound → 404, InvalidPath/OutsideRepoRoot → 400, Other → 500) for seven document routes, and about eighteen blanket `map_err(|_| StatusCode::…)` sites map any error to 500 (`list_issues`, `get_graph`, `get_status`, `search_issues`, `list_gates`, `get_strategic_types`, `get_hierarchy`, `get_namespaces`) or 404 (`get_issue`, `get_gate_definition`, `list_gate_runs`, `get_gate_run`). These disagree with the CLI: `get_issue` reports an IO failure as 404, and `OutsideRepoRoot` is exit 1 in the CLI but 400 over HTTP. The server already depends on `jit` and can call `jit::output::failure::classify(&anyhow::Error) -> JsonError`; document reads return `Result<_, PathReadError>`, which converts with `anyhow::Error::from`. HTTP types stay out of the `jit` crate.

## Success Criteria

- [hard] REQ-01: The server crate holds one function mapping `ErrorCode` to `StatusCode` by an exhaustive `match` with no wildcard arm, so a new code fails to compile until it is mapped.
- [hard] REQ-02: Every route's failure status is that function applied to `classify`'s code for the error; `path_read_error_status` and every blanket `map_err(|_| StatusCode::…)` are gone.
- [hard] REQ-03: Route tests derive expected statuses from the classification of the induced failure, and one owning unit test covers the code-to-status projection.
- [hard] REQ-04: Each route whose status changes for a failure has a test stating the new status, and the remaining server route tests pass without weakened assertions.

## Notes

Where the CLI and the server disagreed today, the classification wins. 0f8efc37 REQ-07 later wraps the handlers in one helper that calls this projection. Embedded static-asset 404s are not error classification and are out of scope. Design rationale: `dev/active/df129d9e-rust-code-quality/plan.md`.
title: Derive server HTTP statuses from the library classification
